audit_findings.title: Legacy landfill obligations may be missing from equity value
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed gross liability of $3.569 billion at 2026-06-30 less $277 million of dedicated trust assets gives a computed provisional net claim of $3.292 billion, equal to 10.7% of base equity value or $8.15 per share; 2025 settlements were $210 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Past landfill obligations may require a bridge deduction unless their cash settlement is already captured as a recurring deduction in owner earnings
audit_findings.evidence: We have significant financial obligations relating to final capping, closure, post-closure and environmental remediation at our existing landfills and we establish accruals for these estimated costs.
audit_findings.explanation: This is not yet a demonstrated bridge error because the $210 million of 2025 settlements and $80 million of first-half 2026 settlements may already reduce operating cash flow and owner earnings. However, the bridge contains no explicit reconciliation, and the provisional net liability is large enough to materially alter the stated intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2025 owner earnings from the cash-flow statement, identify the treatment of landfill and remediation settlements, accretion, revisions and capitalized obligations, and rerun the bridge for only the net claim not represented by recurring cash deductions.

audit_findings.title: Temporary RNG tax credits may be capitalized as perpetual earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: The filed 2025 Section 48 benefit was $184 million, 8.8% of anchor OE; capitalizing that entire amount at the base operating-PV-to-OE ratio would add approximately $2.585 billion or $6.40 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporary tax benefits enter the OE anchor and, if grown into terminal value, inflate forecast OE and the terminal-value base
audit_findings.evidence: We expect our new RNG facilities to qualify for federal tax credits and to realize those credits through 2027 under Section 48 of the Internal Revenue Code.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the $184 million benefit exists and is time-limited, but the supplied valuation does not demonstrate whether it was normalized out. The latest filing also identifies Section 48 credits through 2027 and separate Section 45Z credits through 2029, so a perpetual extrapolation would be materially wrong even though some near-term credits remain valid.
audit_findings.action: Trace Section 48 and Section 45Z benefits through the OE workpaper and rerun the DCF with an explicit annual credit schedule through their disclosed endpoints, including the qualifying capital expenditures required to obtain them.

audit_findings.title: The stakes bridge may double count low-income-housing tax benefits
audit_findings.magnitude: The entire $824 million stakes addition is only 2.69% of base equity value or $2.04 per share; the identified 2026 low-income-housing balances are $577 million of investment and $565 million of related debt
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding a separately valued investment while retaining its tax credits, amortization and financing costs in OE can double count the same economics in the bridge and numerator
audit_findings.evidence: We support the operations of these entities in exchange for a pro-rata share of the tax credits they generate.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting consistency remains unresolved, but even treating the entire $824 million stakes addition as erroneous would change the $75.84 base value by no more than $2.04 per share, versus the $145.88 gap to the $221.72 market price. It therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion on the supplied numbers.
audit_findings.action: Document every component of stakes_net and remove any separately added investment whose tax benefits and financing economics remain in OE; rerun the bridge for audit completeness even though the bounded effect is not conclusion-changing.

audit_findings.title: Emerging PFAS exposure may exceed recorded remediation accruals
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the filed total remediation liability is $230 million at 2026-06-30 and the high end of estimable existing remediation ranges is only $16 million higher, but neither amount isolates PFAS
audit_findings.mechanism: Unaccrued PFAS testing, cleanup and litigation costs could reduce future OE or create an additional claim in the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: Without such relief, we may face increased exposure to remediation and litigation costs associated with properties that the EPA may designate as CERCLA sites due to the presence of PFAS.
audit_findings.explanation: PFAS exposure is a current legal and operational risk, not merely a hypothetical future regulation, but the filings provide no PFAS-specific accrued amount, loss range, site inventory or insurance recovery estimate. The record therefore cannot establish whether the unrecorded exposure is material.
audit_findings.action: Obtain site-level testing results, regulatory notices, probable and reasonably possible loss ranges, insurance exclusions, PRP allocations and Stericycle successor-liability analysis; rerun OE or the bridge if a supportable incremental claim is identified.

audit_findings.title: Stericycle integration costs require explicit normalization
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2025 acquisition and integration costs were $120 million, equal to 5.8% of anchor OE before tax-basis alignment
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing recurring integration spending overstates OE, while retaining genuinely nonrecurring costs understates sustainable OE; synergy assumptions also affect forecast growth and margins
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended December 31, 2025, we incurred acquisition and integration related costs of $120 million, comprised of $89 million of selling, general and administrative costs and $31 million of restructuring costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The supplied valuation does not show whether the $120 million was retained or adjusted. The 2026 filing says restructuring charges became immaterial and reports realized synergies, supporting some normalization, but it does not quantify all remaining integration work or show its treatment in OE. The potential scale is large enough to affect intrinsic value materially, although no error is yet demonstrated.
